correctness.rationale: For every m>=2, a TRD set in F_m has exactly the form apex plus a nonempty union of whole blades: no apex-free set can both totally dominate the peripheral blades and leave the apex nonisolated outside; with apex present, the outside is isolate-free iff no blade is split. This classifies 2-block partitions by subtracting 2^m-1 TRD apex blocks from 4^m choices. For k>=3 any split blade in the apex block would require its unique mate in two distinct partners, impossible; hence the apex block is a singleton and other blocks are unordered unions of whole blades. The resulting bijection yields S(m,k-1), star coalition graphs, unique maximum and Bell total. The exceptional m=1 triangle is treated separately. A separate graph-adjacency implementation checked all vertex subsets and unordered partitions for m=1..5, including every coalition edge; the infinite result follows from the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The theorem naturally and completely classifies a new domination-coalition partition invariant on friendship graphs, not merely one small example: every block-count multiplicity is determined, with a Stirling/Bell spectrum, unique maximal partition and all realizable coalition graphs. The 2024 originating paper explicitly proposed study of associated total restrained coalition graphs; the star-only realization and exact counts address that motivation. The precise friendship-graph family is a standard infinite graph family and the full spectrum is not implied by the preceding scalar graph-class cases.
